headline: Brazil Fines TikTok 153.7 Million Reais
deck: ANPD published a simple fine of R$153,769,671.33 on ByteDance Brasil for five LGPD violations involving children and adolescents. The logged-out feed in Brazil is to carry no ads and a 12-hour cap. ByteDance has ten business days from 24 August notification to appeal.
body: Brazil’s data authority, ANPD, said on 25 August that it had fined ByteDance Brasil Tecnologia Ltda. R$153.7 million for failures in the protection of children’s and adolescents’ data [E1]. The Diário Oficial decision, Despacho Decisório nº 27/2026, sets the exact simple fine at R$153,769,671.33, split across LGPD article 7 and article 6, incisos VIII and X [E2]. ANPD called that five violations [E1]. Notification went out on 24 August [E1][E2].

The logged-out feed is the design fight. ANPD says that in Brazil the unregistered version must suspend ads entirely, limit the session to 12 hours, block creating content, comments, direct messages and live functions, and cut personalisation and data collection to a minimum [E1]. Under-16 accounts are to default to the most restrictive privacy settings, changeable only with a responsible adult’s authorisation [E1]. The operative Diário Oficial text of Despacho 27 itself orders deletion of personal data of adolescents 13–18 whose legal representation is not regularised, plus a technical report [E2]. The 12-hour and ads language sits in the ANPD news note and the approved compliance plan, not in that sanction extract [E1][E2].

Appeal is ten business days from notification, to the Conselho Diretor [E1][E2]. Paying within 20 business days and waiving appeal can cut the fine 25 percent, to R$115,327,253.49 [E2]. TikTok told Brazilian papers the sanction refers to 2021 conduct and does not reflect a 2025 compliance plan already presented to ANPD [E1]. Whether ANPD records an appeal by mid-September is the next public test [E1][E2].
